headline: Yen jumps 1% as AI selloff and $112 oil spark haven bid; peso hits record despite BSP's 50bp
summary: The dollar index eased about 0.1% to near 101.6 as a 2.6% Nasdaq drop on AI doubts and Brent's jump to a five-month high pushed money into Treasuries, cutting the 2-year yield about 17bp to 4.65%. The yen led with a 1% gain, the franc and loonie followed and the won hit a fresh two-year high, while the euro lagged on French debt stress and the peso, rupiah and rupee weakened on oil.
drivers: AI selloff sends money to havens

The Nasdaq fell 2.6% and Meta about 7% on AI-spending doubts, and 2-year Treasury yields dropped about 17bp to 4.65% while the 10-year fell to about 4.96%. USD/JPY fell about 1% to near 156.55 and USD/CHF 0.5% to near 0.8198; futures now see a 22% chance of no further Fed hike this year.

Brent rose about 3% to near $112, a five-month high, after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and reports of planned US–Israeli strikes on Iran. The peso hit a record 63.52 even after the BSP's surprise 50bp hike to 5.50%, the rupee fell 0.4% to about 94.82 and the rupiah 0.2% to 18,060, while oil helped the loonie to a one-month high near 1.4002.

The French–German 10-year spread widened to about 178bp, the most since 2011, on protests and fiscal worries, so the euro slipped about 0.1% to near 1.1222 even as US yields fell. Sterling held near 1.3404, an 18-month high against the euro, on BoE hike bets.
view: Mildly weaker over the next 1–2 weeks against havens and hawkish central banks: Treasury yields have dropped about 40bp from last week's highs, positioning is still long the dollar and a December Fed hike is no longer a lock. I fade the dollar against the yen, franc and Canadian dollar, but back it against the rupiah and peso while oil sits above $110, and French stress keeps the index from falling far below 101.5. Strong US flash PMIs (Oct 23) or a Fed that firmly signals December would take it back toward 102.5; a break below 101.3 opens 101.
ideas: Target 156.80 hit; re-sell rallies into 157.50–157.80 as yields fall and haven demand builds, for 155.00, stop 158.60, about 2.5:1.
BoC hike odds near 75% and oil near $100; sell bounces into 1.4060–1.4080 for 1.3880, stop 1.4160, about 2:1.
BI is easing and MSCI's threat stands; stay long from near 18,000 and add on dips toward 17,950 for 18,250, stop 17,850.
review: USD/JPY's short from 158.50 hit its 156.80 target (about 1.7 yen) and is closed; I take the EUR/USD long off near 1.1222 for about 0.3% as French stress builds, the PHP 63.00–63.50 and EUR/JPY 176–179 ranges broke and are reset, USD/IDR's long from near 18,000 is about 0.3% in favour, USD/TWD's fade is roughly flat, and the CHF, CAD, KRW, SGD and CNH entries were not reached, so I lower the CHF and CAD sell zones.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.1% to near 1.1222 after dipping to about 1.1198 as French spreads hit 2011 wides.

view.call: 1.1150–1.1300; US yields help, France caps rallies.

eurusd.why: France did the damage. The French–German 10-year spread widened to about 178bp, the most since 2011, as President Macron moved to ban protests after weekend riots and fiscal worries spread to other indebted euro members. That offset a 17bp drop in the US 2-year yield to about 4.65%, which would normally lift the euro, so the pair slipped to about 1.1198 before recovering to near 1.1222.
eurusd.outlook: I take the long off near 1.1222 for about 0.3% and move to a 1.1150–1.1300 range: lower US yields help, but French stress has cut ECB hike pricing and caps rallies. A close below 1.1150 would turn me bearish; a French de-escalation would reopen 1.1300.
eurusd.watch: Euro-area flash PMIs (Oct 23), French bond spreads and protests, the Fed (Oct 28) and the ECB (Oct 29).

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.1% to near 1.3404, testing the 1.3410 ceiling; sterling at an 18-month high on the euro.

view.call: 1.3300–1.3450; buy dips, the Oct 28 Budget caps it.

gbpusd.why: Sterling held up better than its peers because rate expectations favour it: a fourth BoE hike in a year is now priced after September's 3.5% CPI beat, while French debt stress has trimmed ECB pricing. The 17bp fall in US 2-year yields helped against the dollar, but the AI-led equity slide and caution before the Oct 28 Budget kept it just under the 1.3408–1.3410 highs.
gbpusd.outlook: Bias stays higher with the BoE set to hike on Nov 5, but I keep trading 1.3300–1.3450 from the bottom until the Budget clears. A daily close above 1.3450 would make me outright bullish; a gilt selloff after the Budget is the risk.
gbpusd.watch: UK flash PMIs (Oct 23), the Budget and the Fed (Oct 28) and the BoE (Nov 5).

audusd.note: Eased about 0.15% to near 0.7018 as the tech selloff hit risk; RBA hike bets kept it above 0.70.
audusd.why: Two forces pulled against each other. The 2.6% fall in the Nasdaq, a 3% drop in Hong Kong stocks and Brent at a five-month high hurt the risk-sensitive Aussie, and copper fell almost 3%. But after Deputy Governor Hauser called the inflation outlook materially worse, markets price roughly a 45–55% chance of a Nov 3 RBA hike and three-year yields rose to about 4.94%, which kept the pair near 0.7018.
audusd.outlook: Range 0.6950–0.7080: RBA hike pricing supports dips, while the AI-led risk selloff limits rallies. Australia's September CPI (Oct 28) decides the break; a close above 0.7080 would turn me bullish.
audusd.watch: Australia flash PMIs (Oct 23), September CPI (Oct 28), yuan fixings and the RBA on Nov 3.

usdjpy.note: Fell about 1% to near 156.55, its lowest since late September; the 158.50 short hit its 156.80 target.

view.call: Sell rallies 157.50–157.80; yields falling, haven bid.

usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving as a haven. The Nasdaq fell 2.6% on AI-spending doubts, Brent jumped about 3% to a five-month high after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, and US 2-year yields dropped about 17bp to 4.65%, narrowing the dollar's rate edge. With positioning long the dollar, a break of 157.50 support and the 50-day average triggered stop-selling to about 156.5, the yen's best day in a month.
usdjpy.outlook: I bank the short at 156.80 and re-sell rallies into 157.50–157.80: the rate gap is narrowing, risk appetite is fragile and Tokyo guards 159–160. Target 155.00, near the early-September low; a close above 158.60, over the 200-day average, would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: Japan September CPI (Oct 23; core seen at 2.1%), US flash PMIs (Oct 23), the Fed (Oct 28) and the BoJ (Oct 30).

usdchf.note: Fell about 0.5% to near 0.8198, a fresh low for the month, on haven demand; the 0.8285 entry was never filled.

view.call: Sell bounces 0.8240–0.8260; haven bid, falling yields.

usdchf.why: Haven demand did the work. The AI-led equity slide, Brent at a five-month high and talk of renewed US–Israeli strikes on Iran sent money into the franc, while a 17–19bp fall in Treasury yields cut the dollar's carry appeal. The franc also gained on the euro as French spreads widened, leaving USD/CHF near 0.8198.
usdchf.outlook: The franc trend is intact, so I lower the sell zone to 0.8240–0.8260 rather than chase, targeting 0.8100. A close above 0.8330 would end the call; an Iran deal and a stock rebound are the main risks.
usdchf.watch: Gulf and Iran headlines, European bond spreads, SNB comments and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdcad.note: Fell about 0.3% to near 1.4002, a one-month low, for a sixth straight loonie gain; 1.4100 wasn't reached.

view.call: Sell bounces 1.4060–1.4080; BoC hike odds near 75%.

usdcad.why: Oil and rate spreads both favoured the loonie. US crude rose about 2% to near $99 after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, lifting Canada's terms of trade, and the 17bp drop in the US 2-year yield narrowed the US–Canada spread while markets price about a 75% chance of a Bank of Canada hike to 2.50% on Oct 28. Canadian September producer prices jumped 2.0% on the month, adding to the hawkish case.
usdcad.outlook: I stay short but lower the sell zone to 1.4060–1.4080, since bounces have been shallow; target the 200-day average near 1.3880. A close above 1.4160 would end the call; a dovish BoC hold is the main risk.
usdcad.watch: Oil and Iran headlines, and the BoC and Fed decisions on Oct 28.

usdcnh.note: Yuan steady near 6.672 offshore; the PBOC fixed 6.7195, 439 pips weaker than estimates.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 6.69; a slow grind at the PBOC's pace.

usdcnh.why: The PBOC kept braking the yuan's rise: the midpoint at 6.7195 was 439 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate, the widest gap since Sept 23. Even so, onshore yuan touched 6.6740, its strongest since June 2022, because the dollar softened against Asia. A 3% slide in Hong Kong stocks and the Shanghai index at a year low kept it from going further.
usdcnh.outlook: A managed grind lower in USD/CNH; I still sell bounces toward 6.69 for 6.64, stop 6.71. Fixes set closer to estimates would speed the move; a deeper China equity selloff would stall it.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings versus estimates, China stock flows, the overnight repo rate and US–China trade headlines.

usdhkd.note: Moved off the 7.85 weak edge to about 7.837 in late quotes as US yields fell.
usdhkd.why: No local catalyst was reported. The most likely driver is the 17bp fall in US 2-year yields, which narrows the gap with HIBOR and makes it less attractive to sell Hong Kong dollars for higher-yielding dollars. That happened even as the Hang Seng fell about 3% and the tech index 5%, so equity flows were not the support.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in a 7.83–7.85 band. A return to 7.85 would force the HKMA to buy HKD and lift HIBOR; a further fall in US yields would keep it off the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: US yields, HKMA action at 7.85, the aggregate balance and one-month HIBOR.

usdsgd.note: Barely moved near 1.2769 as the Singapore dollar tracked the basket.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 1.2800; SGD is low-beta.

usdsgd.why: Offsetting forces left it flat. Lower US yields and a firm yuan supported the Singapore dollar, but the Asian equity selloff and oil at a five-month high hurt regional risk appetite. With the MAS leaving its policy band unchanged on Oct 14 and the S$NEER near the strong side, it moves only a fraction as much as the yen or won.
usdsgd.outlook: Mildly lower if US yields keep falling into the Fed; I'd sell bounces toward 1.2800 for 1.272, stop 1.285. It will lag higher-beta Asian currencies either way.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore September CPI (Oct 23), the broad dollar and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 1.0 to 1,324.2 at the Seoul close, a two-year high for a fifth session, after the BoK held.

view.call: Sell rallies into 1,335–1,340; BoK sees won undervalued.

usdkrw.why: The Bank of Korea held at 3% after two straight hikes but kept further tightening on the table, and Governor Shin said the won is still undervalued on an effective basis, which traders read as tolerance for more gains. That outweighed a 3.5% slide in the Kospi on AI-related profit-taking; the dollar fell from 1,327.5 at the open to 1,324.2, its lowest since Oct 2, 2024.
usdkrw.outlook: The trend still favours the won, so I keep selling rallies into 1,335–1,340 for 1,315 rather than chase it. A foreign exodus from chip stocks is the risk; a close above 1,352 would end the call.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign flows in Seoul, Samsung and SK hynix, Korea's Q3 GDP and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdtwd.note: Taipei close 32.508, up 0.02; markets shut until Oct 27 for Typhoon Champi and a holiday.

view.call: Fade 32.50–32.65; export receipts, central bank caps it.

usdtwd.why: Foreign investors returned to selling, dumping about NT$81.6 billion of Taiwan shares as the Taiex reversed from 47,332 to close 1.8% lower at 46,041, led by MediaTek and Delta Electronics. Selling before a four-day closure for Typhoon Champi added to it. The US dollar traded between 32.450 and 32.642 before closing at 32.508, a small gain; late offshore quotes were nearer 32.60.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep fading the weakness from about 32.55: export receipts are huge and the central bank has said it will act, but renewed foreign selling slows the trade. Target 32.10; a close above 32.80 would stop it.
usdtwd.watch: Taipei reopens Oct 27; foreign flows on the Taiex, TSMC and US big-tech earnings, and central bank action.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0815/0850 at the 6pm close from 4.0790/0825 before the Fed.
usdmyr.why: Caution before next week's Fed meeting dominated. The ringgit opened firmer as the dollar index and US yields fell, but the Asian equity selloff and investors' focus on whether the Fed signals a December hike left it slightly weaker by the close. It fell further against the yen, which outperformed on haven demand.
usdmyr.outlook: Range-bound around 4.07–4.10. Strong exports and talk of Bank Negara tightening support it, but it rarely moves far without the broad dollar.
usdmyr.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, oil prices and Bank Negara's Nov 5 meeting.

usdphp.note: Peso fell 15.9 centavos to a record-low close of 63.52 despite a surprise 50bp BSP hike.
usdphp.why: The BSP raised its rate 50bp to 5.50% when all 27 economists in a Reuters poll expected 25bp, and raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 6% from 5.4%. The peso briefly firmed to about 63.30 but then slid to a record 63.545 intraday, because Brent at a five-month high lifted importers' dollar demand and Governor Remolona said the BSP does not defend the peso, only smooths swings.
usdphp.outlook: The 63.00–63.50 range broke, so I move it up to 63.20–64.00: the hike limits the damage but cannot offset oil, and the BSP only smooths moves. An Iran deal and lower oil would pull it back toward 63.00.
usdphp.watch: Oil and Gulf headlines, BSP dollar sales and the Dec 17 BSP meeting.

usdidr.note: Rupiah weakened 0.21% to 18,060 at the close as the BI hold and MSCI risk weighed.

view.call: Buy dips toward 17,950–18,000; MSCI risk, BI easing.

usdidr.why: The market still read Bank Indonesia's hold at 5.75% and its 2-point cut in reserve requirements as easing, while MSCI's proposal to move Indonesia to standalone status keeps foreign equity money cautious. Higher oil and a Fitch view that growth will stay below the government's target added to the pressure; the dollar's dip elsewhere gave the rupiah no lift.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long the dollar from near 18,000, targeting 18,250, while the MSCI threat stands and BI adds liquidity. A credible government fix for MSCI that pulls it below 17,850 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Foreign flows into Jakarta stocks, the government's response to MSCI, bond auctions and BI intervention.

usdinr.note: Rupee fell 0.4% to about 94.82, ending an eight-day rally, as Brent hit $112.
usdinr.why: Oil turned the rupee. Brent rose about 3% to near $112, a five-month high, after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, and India imports nearly 90% of its crude, so oil importers' dollar demand returned. Weak local stocks added to it; the rupee had touched its best level in over six weeks early before falling to 94.94, and softer US yields only limited the loss.
usdinr.outlook: I shift the range up to 94.30–95.30: Jio IPO inflows and the RBI's limits on oil companies' spot buying cap the dollar, but oil above $110 stops a rupee rally. I wouldn't chase either side.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran headlines, Jio IPO flows, RBI action and foreign portfolio flows.

eurjpy.note: Fell about 1.1% to near 175.7, breaking below the 176–179 range on a broad yen rally.

view.call: Sell rallies 176.50–177.00; France and haven yen.

eurjpy.why: Both legs pushed it lower. The yen rose about 1% against the dollar on haven demand as AI-linked stocks slid and oil hit a five-month high, while the euro lagged on French debt stress, with the French–German spread at its widest since 2011. The yen gained as much as 1.2% on the euro intraday, leaving the cross near 175.7 (EUR/USD 1.1222 × USD/JPY 156.55).
eurjpy.outlook: The range broke lower, so I turn bearish: sell rallies into 176.50–177.00 for 174.00 while France and risk-off weigh. A close above 177.80 would end the call; a French de-escalation is the main risk.
eurjpy.watch: French bond spreads, Japan CPI (Oct 23), and the ECB (Oct 29) and BoJ (Oct 30).

cnhjpy.note: Fell about 1% to near 23.46 as the yen rallied and the yuan held steady.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did all the moving. It rose about 1% against the dollar on haven demand and lower US yields, while the PBOC kept the yuan on a short leash with a fix 439 pips weaker than estimates, so CNH/JPY dropped to about 23.46 (USD/JPY 156.55 divided by USD/CNH 6.672).
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range; it now sits in the lower half. A break below 23.3 would need USD/JPY under about 155.5.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, Japan CPI, the BoJ on Oct 30 and risk sentiment.

watch: Next: Japan CPI, Singapore CPI and flash PMIs (Oct 23), Taipei reopening (Oct 27), Australia CPI, the Fed, BoC and UK Budget (Oct 28), the ECB and BoJ (Oct 29–30), the RBA (Nov 3) and BoE (Nov 5), plus oil, Iran headlines and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
sources: Reuters via Yahoo Finance (yen, dollar, France)
